groups.statement: In the first release, the system shall enable officers to register complaints and start case tracking much faster.
In the first release, the system shall reduce manual paperwork for officers.
In the first release, the system shall reduce delays in sharing information between units.
For records staff, the system shall provide a single place to capture complaint and case details reliably.
The system shall support investigations without requiring repeated re-entry of the same data by records staff.
For citizens, the system shall make complaint submission easier.
For citizens, the system shall provide better visibility that a complaint has been received and is being handled.
The system shall be used in day-to-day police work.
The system shall reduce turnaround time for basic registration tasks.
The system shall improve coordination between police staff and the public.
For the first release, the system shall support in-person complaint submission at the police station.
The system shall provide an online web portal for citizens to file complaints without visiting the police station.
The system shall not exclude any existing complaint submission channel at this stage.
For the first release, station-based complaint entry shall be prioritized before web submission.
A complaint shall start in the submitted or registered state.
A complaint shall move to under review after a records officer or duty officer checks it for completeness and urgency.
If a complaint is valid and actionable, it shall become assigned or under investigation when handed to an investigating officer.
A complaint shall move to closed when the case is resolved.
A complaint shall be escalated if it needs a higher unit.
Each transition shall be governed by authorization and case validity.
Incomplete or duplicate complaints may require clarification before moving forward.
Urgent matters shall be marked for immediate attention.
A complaint shall be closed only after the investigation outcome is recorded.
If a complaint is outside police scope or needs transfer, it shall be formally rejected, referred, or escalated with a reason captured.
For in-person complaints, the officer or records staff shall verify the complainant's identity using a government-issued ID.
For in-person complaints, the officer or records staff shall capture the complainant's basic details against the government-issued ID.
For web portal submissions, the system shall require the citizen to create an account or use a verified login.
For web portal submissions, the system shall require the citizen to provide contact details so the complaint can be traced back if needed.
In the first release, the system shall not require very heavy proof beyond account or verified login and contact details, unless the complaint is very sensitive or high-risk.
If stricter checks are required, the system could require an OTP sent to the registered phone or email.
If stricter checks are required, the system could require supporting documents to be uploaded when available.

A complaint shall be treated as complete if it includes the complainant's basic identity details, a clear description of the incident, the date or approximate time, the location, and enough information to understand what happened.
A complaint shall be treated as valid if it is within police scope and contains enough facts to start an entry.
If key details are missing, the system shall mark the complaint as incomplete and send it back for clarification rather than pushing it into investigation.

For duplicate detection, the system shall compare the complainant's name or contact information, the incident date, the location, and a summary of the allegation against existing complaints and open cases.
If the system identifies a likely duplicate match, it shall flag the complaint for human review instead of auto-closing it.
After human review, staff may merge the complaint, link it, or mark it as a duplicate with a reason.
Citizens shall only be able to create their own complaints.
Citizens shall be able to view the status of their own submissions.
Citizens shall be able to add follow-up information that is requested or allowed.
Citizens shall not be able to see internal notes.
Citizens shall not be able to see officer assignments.
Citizens shall not be able to see investigation details.
Citizens shall not be able to see other citizens' records.
Records staff shall be able to create complaints.
Records staff shall be able to search complaints.
Records staff shall be able to verify completeness.
Records staff shall be able to update basic registration details.
Records staff shall be able to route cases.
Records staff shall not be able to close investigations.
Records staff shall not be able to alter substantive case findings.
Investigating officers shall be able to view assigned cases.
Investigating officers shall be able to update assigned cases.
Investigating officers shall be able to add investigation notes.
Investigating officers shall be able to escalate cases when needed.
Investigating officers shall be able to close cases when appropriate.
Access to sensitive records shall be limited by role.
Access to sensitive records shall be limited by station or jurisdiction when necessary.
A station shall be able to fully work only on its own registered cases unless there is an approved transfer or escalation.
Any transfer or sharing shall leave an audit trail and include the reason.
Only supervisors or designated administrators shall approve complaint movements across areas.
